query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents (hardware vs software vs printer vs network) is directly central to explaining a hardware incident spike, enabling grouping and comparison within the anomaly window. Sample values (software installs -> software, MySQL connection -> database) are sound readings of short_description.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure modes (not_powering_on, overheating, physical_damage, connectivity_failure) give a genuine new axis to diagnose WHY hardware failed during the spike -- highly relevant. Values appear warranted from descriptions; NULL/Unknown for silent rows (e.g. generic software install) is appropriate behavior, not a hallucination.

per_column.name: software_update_triggered
per_column.rationale: A near-constant boolean (578 false / 22 true) with a bare flag character limits leverage, though a software-update trigger could plausibly relate to a hardware spike root cause. Values look conservatively inferred and 'update' descriptions are not force-flagged true, so grounding is reasonable.

per_column.name: incident_action_type
per_column.rationale: Action type (hardware_repair_replacement, connectivity_repair, installation) partially overlaps with incident_category but adds a resolution/action axis useful for characterizing the spike's workload. Sample mappings are well grounded in the text.

per_column.name: recurring_caller
per_column.rationale: This is largely a restatement of the existing caller_id column (just surfacing top callers), adding little new analytical axis. Labeling callers as 'recurring' is a distinct claim requiring frequency evidence; a single-row sample cannot confirm recurrence, so specific attributions are weakly grounded.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: A recurrence flag is genuinely useful for explaining a spike (repeat incidents driving volume). However, recurrence is not derivable from a single row's source_text; the true/false determination depends on cross-row logic not evidenced in samples, making per-row grounding uncertain.

judge.rationale: Most columns give real analytical leverage for diagnosing a hardware spike -- incident_category and failure_mode are directly on-point, and incident_action_type/recurrence_signal add useful axes. recurring_caller largely duplicates caller_id and, like recurrence_signal, asserts frequency/recurrence claims not verifiable from single-row source text. Category/failure_mode/action mappings are well grounded with appropriate Unknown handling for silent rows; the recurrence-based columns are the main grounding weakness.
